_comment: SHARED cross-language corpus for the wiki-link bracket grammar (BUG-2834).
GENERATED FILE -- pure ASCII by construction. Every control character and
non-ASCII code point below is a \uXXXX escape, never a raw byte, so this
file survives editors, diffs, terminals and copy-paste intact. An early
probe for this very bug typed U+2028/U+2029 into a shell heredoc, silently
lost them, and would have 'confirmed' the divergence on two cases that were
actually spaces. Do not hand-edit a raw control character into this file.
Consumed by BOTH implementations of the grammar, which are written as the
same pattern text in two languages that do not agree on what it means:
Go: internal/links/extract.go      wikiLinkPattern
asserted by internal/links/grammar_parity_test.go
JS: web/src/lib/utils/markdown.ts  renderMarkdown + wikiLinksToMarkdown
asserted by web/src/lib/utils/markdown.grammarParity.test.ts
THE POINT: neither implementation defines truth. The `expect` fields are
derived from the grammar SPEC and both languages are asserted against them,
so a divergence introduced on EITHER side fails on that side. This file
exists because the two patterns are BYTE-IDENTICAL SOURCE TEXT -- a reviewer
comparing them side by side concludes they agree, and BUG-2834 lived in the
gap between that reading and the host languages' definition of `.`.
THE SPEC. The body production is `(?:\\.|[^\]\\])+` where `.` means ANY
CHARACTER EXCEPT LINE FEED (U+000A) -- Go's RE2 definition. JavaScript's `.`
additionally excludes CR, U+2028 and U+2029, which IS the divergence; the JS
patterns therefore spell it `[^\n]` explicitly rather than `.`.
`content` is the FULL input string. `expect.match` is whether the grammar
matches anywhere in it; `expect.body` is capture group 1 of the FIRST match
and is absent when match is false.

cases.name: plain body
cases.why: baseline: the ordinary form must match in both languages

cases.name: pipe display segment
cases.why: the `|` display separator is an ordinary body byte to the grammar

cases.name: escaped close bracket
cases.why: the `\\.` alternative's primary job: `\]` must not terminate the body

cases.name: escaped pipe
cases.why: escapeWikiBody emits `\|` for a literal pipe in a title

cases.name: escaped backslash
cases.why: escapeWikiBody doubles backslashes first; the pair must be one unit

cases.name: empty body
cases.why: the production is `+`, so an empty body is not a link

cases.name: escaped close consumes the first of a bare pair
cases.why: `[[A\]]` has nothing left to close with -- the naive strings.Index scan got this wrong (BUG-2805)

cases.name: escaped close then real close
cases.why: `[[A\]]]` closes on the LAST two brackets, body keeps the escape

cases.name: trailing backslash with nothing to consume
cases.why: `\\.` needs a byte after the backslash; there is none

cases.name: surplus closing brackets
cases.why: the match ends at the first legal close; the extra `]]` is outside it

cases.name: inner open brackets are ordinary body bytes
cases.why: `[` is not excluded by `[^\]\\]`, so the body swallows it -- checks greediness agrees across RE2 and backtracking

cases.name: raw LF inside body
cases.why: a RAW line terminator is matched by the `[^\]\\]` alternative in BOTH languages -- this is why `.` excluding them was never a deliberate rule about titles

cases.name: raw CR inside body
cases.why: same as raw LF: the second alternative admits it, so only the ESCAPED form ever diverged

cases.name: backslash before LF
cases.why: BUG-2834 control: Go's `.` excludes LF, so this is NOT an escape pair and the bracket fails -- both languages already agreed here, and the fix must not change it (scanBracketBody in links.go depends on it)

cases.name: backslash before CR
cases.why: BUG-2834 divergence 1 of 3: Go matched, JS did not. CRLF line endings make this the plausible one -- a body ending in a backslash immediately before a CRLF break

cases.name: backslash before U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR
cases.why: BUG-2834 divergence 2 of 3: excluded by ECMAScript's LineTerminator, not by RE2's

cases.name: backslash before U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR
cases.why: BUG-2834 divergence 3 of 3

cases.name: backslash before U+000B VERTICAL TAB
cases.why: BOUNDS the divergence: a vertical whitespace control that is NOT an ECMAScript LineTerminator. Agreement here is what makes the population exactly three rather than 'the whitespace controls'

cases.name: backslash before U+000C FORM FEED
cases.why: BOUNDS the divergence: same role as VT

cases.name: backslash before U+0085 NEXT LINE
cases.why: BOUNDS the divergence: a Unicode line break that ECMAScript does NOT count as a LineTerminator. The 'it is all Unicode line breaks' hypothesis dies here

cases.name: backslash before space
cases.why: ordinary escape of a non-special byte: legal in both, and the negative control for the divergence cases above

cases.name: backslash before tab
cases.why: ordinary escape, horizontal whitespace

cases.name: collection-qualified body
cases.why: the `<slug>/<title>` form is ordinary body text to the GRAMMAR -- the ambiguity it creates is BUG-2830's, decided above the grammar, not inside it

cases.name: cross-workspace form
cases.why: `::` is likewise ordinary body text to the grammar
